briefing_2026-10-13_enso_forecast: A strong El Nino is in place and forecast to persist, with the relative Nino3.4 index having risen from +0.8 C in May to about +2.5 C in August and September. The ACCESS-S2 run of 10 October takes the ensemble mean to about +3.4 C in October and a peak near +3.7 C in November and December, before a decline to about +3.0 C in February and +2.4 C in March 2027. Every member stays far above the +0.8 C El Nino threshold through March and the spread is small, roughly half a degree around the mean.
briefing_2026-10-13_enso_observed: The relative Nino3.4 index stood at +2.76 C in the week to 11 October 2026, far above the +0.8 C El Nino threshold and still rising. The index climbed steeply from about -0.8 C in early 2026, crossed the El Nino threshold around June, and now clearly exceeds the previous peak of about +1.6 C reached in late 2023.
briefing_2026-10-13_iod_forecast: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole is established and forecast to peak in the coming weeks, with the index up from -0.2 C in May to about +0.65 C in September. The ACCESS-S2 run of 10 October puts the ensemble mean at +1.0 C in October and about +1.1 C in November, easing to +0.85 C in December and dropping below the +0.4 C positive threshold in January 2027, then near +0.1 C in February and March. Member spread in November is wide, from about +0.6 to +1.7 C, but nearly all members stay positive through December.
briefing_2026-10-13_iod_observed: The IOD index was +0.88 C in the week to 11 October 2026, above the +0.4 C positive threshold and at its highest value of the year. The index has risen from about -0.4 C in mid 2026 after a short positive spell earlier in the year, and follows a strongly negative event that bottomed out near -2.0 C in November 2025.
briefing_2026-10-13_olr_map_africa: Observed 7-day OLR anomalies show enhanced convection over the Sahel and northern Africa between 10N and 25N from 21 September to 4 October, shifting to West Africa and the eastern Atlantic in the week of 5 to 11 October, with suppressed convection over the Arabian Sea east of 60E throughout. The CFS forecast for 12 to 18 October places strongly enhanced convection (-42 to -54 W m-2) over the western equatorial Indian Ocean near 5N between 60E and 80E, associated with MJO and equatorial Rossby wave contours. That centre moves south of the equator near 60E for 19 to 25 October with strong suppression east of 80E, and anomalies over Africa are weak from 26 October to 8 November.
briefing_2026-10-13_hovmoller_olr_tropic: OLR anomalies averaged over 15S to 15N show persistent enhanced convection over the central and eastern Pacific between about 180 and 110W since late July, with suppressed convection over the Indian Ocean and Maritime Continent between 60E and 150E, a low-frequency pattern consistent with El Nino. Over Africa and the western Indian Ocean (0 to 60E) anomalies have been weak, with brief Kelvin wave activity around 25 September to 2 October. The CFS forecast from 9 October keeps suppression over the eastern Indian Ocean near 80E to 110E through late October, with only weakly enhanced convection near 60E in mid October and continued enhancement over the central Pacific.
